admin:/cases/trends.purpose: Complaint Intelligence shows where complaints come from, what causes them and which ones need management now. Managers use it to find root causes and stop the same problem coming back.
steps: Read the tiles **Complaints**, **Being worked**, **Awaiting family**, **Reopened**, **Repeat** and **Avg to resolve**.
Read **Summary for management** for a short written overview of the month. It is refreshed once a day.
Read **Needs management attention** for escalated, reopened and overdue complaints. Press a case number to open it.
Read **Rising this month** for complaint types growing against last month, and **People with recurring complaints** for teachers or staff named in more than one complaint.
Read **Response deadlines** and **Confirmation calls overdue** to chase cases that are late or still waiting for the family's answer.
Read **Complaints received and closed by month** to see whether the backlog is growing or shrinking.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
The person a complaint is about never sees it here or anywhere else.
Complaint history for a named employee is only shown to the people allowed to see it, and every look is recorded in the audit log.

admin:/cases/settings.purpose: Complaint Settings holds the escalation ladder and the parent-confirmation rules. Senior management uses it to decide who a complaint goes to next and when a case may close without the family's answer.
steps: Under **Escalation ladder** put the roles in order, from the first person who handles a complaint to the last. The default is Academy Manager, Head of Admissions, Head of People, then Super Admin.
Under **Parent confirmation** set **Days to confirm with the family** and **Unanswered attempts before a manager may close**.
Write a **Rationale** for the change and press **Save settings**.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
A resolved complaint goes to the family for confirmation. If the family is not satisfied, the case reopens and moves one step up the ladder.
Every change is recorded in the audit log with its rationale.

admin:/academics/student-summary.purpose: The Monthly Student Summary shows every student on one page for one month: classes, absences, late arrivals, lessons completed, class content, assessments and open follow-ups. Students needing attention come first.
steps: Choose the **Month**, and if you want, a **Teacher** or a **Student** name, then press **Go**.
Read the tiles **Students**, **Classes held**, **Attended**, **Absences**, **Late arrivals**, **Lessons completed** and **Need attention**.
Read the flags on each row, for example **No progress recorded** or many absences.
Press a student name or **Open** to see that student's Academic Journey for the month.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
No progress recorded means no lesson was marked complete and no class content was written in the month.
Academic managers receive this summary by email at the start of each month.

teacher:/academics/student-summary.purpose: The Monthly Student Summary shows your own students for one month: classes, absences, late arrivals, lessons completed, class content, assessments and open follow-ups.
steps: Choose the **Month** and press **Go**.
Read the tiles and the flags on each row. Students needing attention are at the top.
Press a student name or **Open** to see the student's Academic Journey for the month.
notes: You only see the students you teach.
If a student shows **No progress recorded**, write the class content and mark lessons complete after each class.

admin:/parent-contacts.purpose: The Parent Contact Log records every conversation with a family: what was said, what was agreed, who follows up and by when. Academic and admissions staff use it so nothing a parent says is lost.
steps: Read the tiles **This month**, **Follow-ups open**, **Mine to do**, **Overdue**, **Issues identified** and **Referrals mentioned**. Press a tile to filter.
Filter by **Search**, **About**, **Staff**, **Follow-up**, **From** or **To** and press **Go**.
Press **Record a conversation**. Fill **Who and when**, **What was said** and **Issue and follow-up**. Attach a recording or paste a transcript if you have one.
If the family mentioned someone who may want to join, fill **Referral**. A new lead is created for the admissions team.
Press **Save the conversation**. Press **Open** on a row to read it, complete the follow-up or raise a complaint from it.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
A follow-up becomes a task for the person named. They are reminded on the due date and their manager is told when it is overdue.
If the family is upset or concerned, the conversation can be turned into a complaint in one step.
Referral rewards are given as credit only, and only after a person approves them.

admin:/attention.purpose: Needs Attention brings together the students, teachers and families that a daily check has flagged. Every item says why it was flagged, and nothing happens until a person decides.
steps: Read the tiles **Open**, **High**, **Students**, **Teachers**, **Referral opportunities** and **Actions approved**. Press a tile to filter.
Use the tabs **Students**, **Teachers**, **Referral opportunities**, **Decided** and **Resolved**. Filter by level or by finding and press **Filter**.
Read the one-line summary on each item. Press **Why, and what to do** to see the findings and the recommended actions.
Tick the actions you agree with, add a note if needed, and press **Approve and assign**. Each action becomes a task for its owner with a due date.
Or choose a number of days and press **Snooze**, or write why nothing is needed and press **Dismiss**.
Press **Check now** to run the check again straight away.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
The check looks at attendance, absences, late arrivals, progress, syllabus pace, teacher changes, complaints, assessments, overdue follow-ups, parent calls and retention risk.
A dismissed item only comes back if something new is found. An item resolves itself when its findings clear.
A supervisor sees only the students and teachers they supervise. Teacher items are for management only.

admin:/admin/integrations/ghl/sync.purpose: GoHighLevel Sync shows what moves between GoHighLevel and the ERP. GHL runs leads, marketing and the sales pipeline; the ERP owns families, students and academics.
steps: Under **Connection** check whether sync is on. Press **Turn sync on** or **Turn sync off**.
Read the tiles **Waiting to send**, **Sent (24h)**, **Received (24h)**, **Retrying**, **Failed for good** and **Conflicts to review**.
Filter the list by **Search**, **Direction**, **Record** or **Status** and press **Go**. Press **Retry** on a failed row, or **Retry everything that failed**.
Press **Send due changes now** to send waiting changes straight away.
Under **Conflicts to review** compare **In the ERP** with **From GHL**, write a **Rationale**, then press **Keep the ERP values (update GHL)** or **Take the GHL values**.
Read **Pipeline stages** to match each ERP stage to its GHL stage id, and **Webhooks to add in GHL** for the addresses GHL must call.
notes: This page is an addition to the original ERP.
Sync is off until it is turned on here. Without GHL credentials on the server, changes are simulated and nothing leaves the server.
A failed change is retried six times over about 18 hours. After that it is marked failed for good and an alert is raised.
